extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: A dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task, requiring broad discourse context.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bemardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.citeAs: Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, pages 1525–1534, Berlin, Germany, August 7-12, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The LAMBADA data come from the Book Corpus. Passages were filtered using language models to remove easy cases. Remaining passages were evaluated by human subjects via CrowdFlower crowdsourcing in three steps: guessing the target word from the whole passage, verifying with a second subject, and ensuring the word could not be guessed from the last sentence alone by up to 10 subjects.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), containing unpublished novels.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The Book Corpus was filtered for duplicate removal and potentially offensive material. Passages were filtered using four language models to exclude those where the target word had a probability >= 0.00175. The novels were randomly divided into training and development+testing partitions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal, filtering out potentially offensive material with a stop word list, filtering out passages guessable by standard language models, and splitting novels into disjoint training, development, and testing sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects guessed the target word based on the whole passage (steps 1 and 2) and then based on the target sentence only (step 3). A passage was included if two consecutive subjects guessed the word correctly from the full context, and no subject out of ten could guess it from the last sentence alone.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The criteria for inclusion were strict: two consecutive subjects had to exactly match the missing word, and no subject could provide it based on local context only. An alternative approach allowing plausible/synonymous continuations was deemed not financially or practically feasible.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple (at least 2 for context, up to 10 for sentence-only condition)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN), standard 4-gram model, feed-forward model
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development set and training corpus are available for download. The test set was planned to be made available at the time of a public competition.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to encourage the development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text, moving beyond statistical generalizations.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely overrepresented in LAMBADA (48%) compared to the input data. The dataset contains direct speech significantly more often than the input items overall.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging by design, as it filters out passages that standard language models can solve. It focuses on broad discourse context, which may not represent all aspects of text understanding. The strict hit-or-miss annotation criteria may exclude passages with plausible alternative answers.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing, Validation, Benchmarking. It is meant to evaluate general-purpose models in terms of how they fare on broad-context understanding.
